Version: Latest version patched to allow only image file types GIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG by default
Method of Attack: Allowed attacker to upload arbitrary files on web servers including command shells
Exploited flaw caused by Apache 2.3.9 disabling .htaccess files by default, which ignored folder-related security settings
Uploading PHP shells via proof-of-concept exploits targeting forks and variations
Impacted Systems: Web servers using jQuery File Upload plugin and its forks
Attack Vector: Uploading malicious files through the jQuery File Upload widget exploiting lack of folder access restrictions
Indicators of Compromise: Vulnerable forks of jQuery File Upload plugin (over 7,800 variations, with many vulnerable)
Proof-of-concept exploits and YouTube videos demonstrating exploitation since at least 2015
